children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar before Fed Chairman Warsh's fireside chat at an IMF event in Bangkok today. "Following upside data surprises this week, market participants will closely watch" his fireside chat for any signals regarding the Fed's October meeting, CBA's Carol Kong says in a research report. "Given Warsh's distaste for forward guidance, he might subtly signal his preference for the October rate outcome," the economist and currency strategist adds. The U.S. dollar rises 0.3% to 1,344.80 won, but is steady at 1.2822 Singapore dollars, while the Australian dollar is little changed at US$0.6920, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
